domain: DeepSeek Harness architecture, operations, extension development, security, testing, and debugging
refresh_cadence: on every upstream release or architecture change, and monthly while developer preview continues

sources.title: DeepSeek Harness source repository at pinned commit
claims: The reviewed checkout is version 0.1.1-rc.2 at commit b150a551b8d465e31e418e1b2eaf5e79bbb7d28e.
The repository is an MIT-licensed developer-preview agent harness maintained by DeepSeek AI.
The tracked repository contains TypeScript, Python, native, Web, documentation, example, and vendored Cordis surfaces.

sources.title: DeepSeek Harness README
claims: DeepSeek Harness describes itself as an open-source agent harness where everything is a plugin.
The project is in developer preview and explicitly allows compatibility-breaking changes.
The documented source workflow is pnpm install, pnpm run build, then pnpm dsh web.

sources.title: DeepSeek Harness repository agent instructions
claims: New behavior belongs on documented plugin extension points rather than in the agent loop.
Model-visible inputs must be reconstructable from the session log.
Registrations are reversible effects and capability seams require definition, provider, and consumer roles.

sources.title: DeepSeek Harness architecture
claims: Profiles stack bundles and patch layers over an initially empty Cordis entry list.
Session events are durable facts while agent and capability events control live work.
The core turn flow admits input, assembles prompt and tools, streams a model request, executes tools, and closes the turn.

sources.title: Agent turn and step lifecycle
claims: A step contains one model request plus its tools, while a turn contains zero or more steps.
The pre-step decision may reject the proposed step or replace the complete entered message batch.
SDK transcript consumers should use session events, while agent events are the live coordination API.

sources.title: Capability seams and core services
claims: The generated capability graph distinguishes service declarations, providers, and direct consumers.
Provider replacement changes all consumers behind the same service interface.
Filesystem, subprocess, sandbox, approval, LLM, persistence, and subagents are separate services.

sources.title: Tool execution pipeline
claims: Tool execution runs pre-execute policy, monotonic guards, execution, post-execute rewriting, finalization, and immutable result observation.
Approval resolves one-shot asks before monotonic owner guards.
A single tool result is the model-facing outcome after pipeline normalization and finalization.

sources.title: Defensive lifecycle and concurrency patterns
claims: Orthogonal outcomes such as timeout, signal, and exit code must be reported independently.
Disposal must reach quiescence rather than merely request cancellation.
Spawned commands receive a scrubbed environment and private unpredictable temporary paths.

sources.title: DeepSeek Harness testing policy
claims: Unit, coverage, real-API, transcript snapshot, and browser snapshot tiers prove different things.
The coverage gate requires per-file 100 percent on package source but is explicitly insufficient by itself.
Product-visible plugins require a real Loader composition test and built entrypoints require built-artifact smokes.

sources.title: DeepSeek Harness development guide
claims: The repository supports Node 22.19 and later in the 22 line, plus Node 24 and later, with pnpm 11.7.0.
Host and Client compile as separate TypeScript aggregate programs because their Cordis Context merges would collide.
Built-artifact consumers require a preceding build.

sources.title: DeepSeek Harness base bundle composition
claims: The shipped base profile defaults to workspace-write sandbox mode and ask approval unless explicitly overridden.
Danger-full-access pairs an unrestricted sandbox mode with never-ask approval.
The base composition mounts service, policy, provider, tool, persistence, compaction, subagent, workflow, and Web-search rows.

sources.title: Concrete agent-loop package contract
claims: Agent creation and resume use rollback-covered publication with owned teardown.
Followup, steer, and inject differ by target inbox and wake behavior.
Parallel-safe tool bodies may overlap, while policy and durable results remain model ordered.

sources.title: DeepSeek Harness Cordis primer
claims: Cordis supplies the context, plugin, service, event, scope, and effect substrate used by the Harness.
Effect ownership and disposal are central to dynamic plugin correctness.

sources.title: Vendored Cordis package provenance table
claims: The repository records upstream package versions and local vendored package paths.
The recorded upstream Cordis baseline is 4.0.0-rc.7 while the local cordis manifest is 4.0.1.

sources.title: Vendored Cordis Fiber lifecycle implementation
claims: The local Fiber implements explicit lifecycle state, effect ownership, child scopes, and quiescent disposal behavior.

sources.title: Vendored loader configuration reconciliation
claims: Configuration changes prepare and settle candidate state before committing it.
Failure attempts restoration, but restoration can also fail, so the behavior is rollback-covered rather than strictly atomic.

sources.title: Vendored include and YAML configuration loader
claims: The configuration surface supports JavaScript-valued YAML tags and must be treated as trusted configuration input.

sources.title: Session event runtime
claims: Session append validates contiguous sequence and stores immutable JSON event snapshots.
Model messages are derived from the committed event history.

sources.title: Agent request reconstruction invariant
claims: The agent loop checks that each model-visible request can be reconstructed from session evidence.

sources.title: Tool registry and execution runtime
claims: Tool registration is reversible and duplicate names are rejected.
Policy denial prevents the tool body from executing and produces one normalized final result.

sources.title: System prompt and tool-schema assembly runtime
claims: Prompt sections and effective tool schemas are assembled through ordered, disposable contributions.

sources.title: Provider-neutral LLM service runtime
claims: Prepared model calls bind an adapter route before dispatch and expose a provider-neutral stream contract.

sources.title: Session persistence service contract
claims: Persistence exposes explicit append, load, and flush semantics.
The contract must not be restated as crash durability without provider-specific evidence.

sources.title: User approval service runtime
claims: Approval uses one-shot decisions with explicit policy and cancellation behavior.

sources.title: Sandbox service contract
claims: The sandbox contract reports per-call mode, root, and enforcement evidence.
File-effect confinement is not by itself a complete hostile-code isolation guarantee.

sources.title: Subagent service runtime
claims: Subagent providers publish bounded runs with typed results, ownership, and disposal behavior.

sources.title: API gateway request dispatcher
claims: The gateway separates request dispatch from transport ownership and uses explicit result and error behavior.
